text:
Arttu Hyry is the kind of story that gets written about: an undrafted Finn from Oulu, on an $875,000 contract, studying engineering while he plays about 15 minutes a night in Dallas. The Dallas News called him "a breakout Star on the ice," and the numbers mostly agree.

Five goals in 22 games is fine. What's better is how he gets them. He has 5.77 expected goals (1.07 per 60, up from 0.86 last season), and he has actually scored a little below that. Over the last 10 games he generated 3.4 expected goals on his own. His shot is a weapon, 95 mph at the top end (98th percentile), and the Stars take 53% of the expected goals at five on five with him on.

The caveats are about sample. Last season was 236 minutes, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has only eight of his games, so nothing there stands out yet. But a player whose chances run ahead of his goals is a player whose goals tend to catch up. Our range has him around 19 goals by season's end.
